title: Victorian collar shawlette
subtitle: A small scallop-lace collar shawlette in fingering-weight cotton, adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet
excerpt: This collar shawlette works a scalloped lace edging in fingering-weight cotton on a 3 mm hook. Each scallop unit is dc, ch 3, sl st, repeated across the row, with a shallow curve built by short-row shaping on the straight upper edge. Finished size is approximately 80 cm wide by 25 cm deep. The pattern is adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet (1886).
sourceNotes: Collar shawlette construction and scallop edging adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 1 (1886), 'A Crochet Collar' and 'Scalloped Edging' chapters (Internet Archive). Adapted for fingering-weight cotton; original used white crochet thread.

glossaryTerms.definition: A repeating decorative unit consisting of 1 dc, ch 3, and 1 sl st worked back into the base of the ch-3, forming a small looped point. Scallop units sit side by side along the lower edge of this shawlette.

Working partway across a row and turning before reaching the end, to add extra length to one part of the fabric. Here it builds extra depth at the centre back so the shawlette curves to sit on the shoulders.

content.text: This collar shawlette sits close to the shoulders and neck in the style of the decorative lace collars found in Weldon's Practical Crochet from 1886. The body is worked in rows of double crochet with short-row shaping to build extra depth at the centre back. A row of scallop units runs along the lower edge and the two front ends. Fingering-weight cotton on a 3 mm hook gives a fine, crisp fabric that holds the collar shape without stiffening.
The
scallop unit
is: 1 dc into the fabric, ch 3, sl st into the base of the ch-3. This forms one small pointed loop. Work these across the lower edge with 3 dc between each scallop. The
short-row shaping
in the body ensures the straight upper edge curves to follow the shoulder line rather than sitting flat.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 100 g fingering-weight cotton yarn. A 3 mm crochet hook (US C/2 or D/3). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Blocking mat. Blocking pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge
22 dc x 26 rows = 10 x 10 cm in fingering-weight cotton with a 3 mm hook, measured unstretched. The collar is a small piece so accurate gauge is essential for the finished 80 cm width.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
picot (ch 3, sl st to base of chain): used in scallop units.
Pattern

The shawlette is worked from the straight upper edge downward. The foundation chain is the full 80 cm width. Short rows add extra depth at the centre of the piece. The scallop border is worked separately along the lower edge once the body is complete.
Foundation chain
Ch 177. (This gives 176 working stitches across the 80 cm width.)
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch throughout). 1 dc in each ch across. Turn. (176 sts)
Rows 2 to 10 (full rows)
Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in each st across. Turn. (176 sts each row)
Short rows: building centre depth
Short row A: Ch 1. 1 dc in each of next 88 sts (centre half of the row). Turn. Do not work to the end of the row. (88 sts worked)
Short row B: Ch 1. 1 dc in each of the 88 sts just worked. Turn. (88 sts)
Short row C: Ch 1. 1 dc in each of next 66 sts (centre third). Turn. (66 sts worked)
Short row D: Ch 1. 1 dc in each of the 66 sts just worked. Turn. (66 sts)
Rows 11 to 16 (full rows)
Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in each st across the full 176 sts. Turn. (176 sts each row)
Scallop border

Do not fasten off. Work the scallop border along the lower (row 16) edge, then down each short front end. Starting at the bottom-right corner: *1 dc in next st, ch 3, sl st into the base of the ch-3 just made (1 scallop unit formed), 1 dc in each of next 3 sts*; repeat from * to * across the full lower edge. Work 1 dc into each row-end along the right front, then the same scallop sequence down the right front. Mirror for the left front if desired. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 10 minutes, pressing out excess water, and pinning to 80 x 25 cm on a blocking mat with the scallop points individually pinned outward. Leave until fully dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Cotton can be lightly pressed with a damp cloth and a cool iron to restore crispness. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

Work a second row of scallops offset from the first for a deeper, more layered border. Replace the dc body with an open filet grid (dc and ch-1 alternating) for a lighter, lace-like collar. A small button and loop at each front corner holds the shawlette in place when worn.
